name: bulkcap
description: The control for 11.2's unimpaired cells. `bulk-iperf3` lets iperf3 send as fast as it can, which on a one-vCPU lab host means the `clean` and `lan` cells measure the host's core rather than the protocol: every process in the box, both tunnel ends, iperf3's client and its server, competes for the same CPU, so whichever implementation costs less per byte simply wins, and the goodput column reads as a protocol result when it is an efficiency result. Capping the offered rate at 250 Mbit/s, comfortably below the lowest rate any pair reached uncapped, makes every pair deliver the same bits, and the interesting column becomes CPU per delivered bit rather than Mbit/s. That is the only form in which `clean` says anything about the protocol, and it is the like-for-like comparison D29's accepted flush cost has to be read from. Identical to `bulk-iperf3` in every other respect, so the two are directly comparable cell by cell.
